title: Word Break
statement: Given a string `s` and a dictionary of words, return `True` if `s` can be cut into a sequence of dictionary words. A word may be used more than once.

example.why: "cats" + "and". (Starting with "cat" leaves "sand", which is not a word — the DP still finds the other cut.)

idea: Let `dp[i]` say whether the **first i letters** can be cut into dictionary words. `dp[0]` is True: the empty prefix needs no words.
The first `i` letters can be cut if there is some position `j` where the part before it works (`dp[j]` is True) **and** the remaining piece `s[j:i]` is a word.
Fill `dp` from left to right. `dp[len(s)]` answers the question for the whole string.

complexity.timeWhy: There are about n² pairs (j, i), and cutting out the piece `s[j:i]` and looking it up costs up to O(n) more.
complexity.spaceWhy: The dp array (plus the word set).

steps.text: Our example: **`s = "catsand", wordDict = ["cats","and","cat"]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`dp[i]` answers: can the first i letters be cut into words? For 0 letters: yes, trivially.
